executiveSummary: Surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning October 2025 through May 2026 reveal multiple concurrent threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity in the Americas has generated repeated alerts (November 2025 and March 2026), representing a critical zoonotic spillover risk with pandemic potential. Mpox continues circulating in the Americas region, while dengue, chikungunya, and yellow fever maintain elevated transmission. Seasonal respiratory virus co-circulation including influenza, RSV, and pertussis resurgence compounds healthcare system pressures across multiple regions.
bottomLine: Concurrent H5N1 zoonotic spillover risk, mpox spread, and multi-pathogen respiratory season activity represent the dominant threats requiring coordinated surveillance and response across the Americas and Europe.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Repeated PAHO epidemiological updates in November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained regional activity
Zoonotic spillover risk with pandemic potential given ongoing animal-human interface exposure
BSL-3 select agent with high case fatality rate in confirmed human cases
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interfaces; enforce PPE protocols for farm and wildlife workers; sequence isolates for antigenic drift; coordinate with FAO and WHO on cross-border animal movement monitoring

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 indicating ongoing regional transmission
BSL-3 select agent with sustained human-to-human transmission capability
Continued spread across multiple countries in the Americas requiring alert-level response
threats.action: Strengthen contact tracing and case isolation; expand vaccination access in high-risk populations; enhance laboratory diagnostic capacity; coordinate with ECDC on cross-regional case tracking

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating renewed transmission risk
BSL-3 select agent with high case fatality rate in unvaccinated populations
Epizootic activity in non-human primates is an early warning indicator of human spillover risk
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in endemic zones; enhance vector surveillance; issue travel health advisories; ensure vaccine stockpile adequacy for outbreak response

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 2026 indicates high case burden continuing from record 2024-2025 surge
Multiple serotype co-circulation increases severe dengue risk
Expanded Aedes aegypti vector range driven by climate factors
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations in high-burden urban areas; strengthen severe dengue case management; monitor serotype distribution through genomic surveillance; prepare healthcare surge capacity

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two consecutive PAHO alerts in December 2025 and March 2026 indicate sustained resurgence
Waning immunity from vaccination and potential vaccine-escape strains driving increased case counts
High vulnerability in unvaccinated infants and immunocompromised populations
threats.action: Review vaccination coverage data and close gaps; promote booster doses for adolescents, adults, and pregnant women; enhance neonatal protection protocols; investigate potential macrolide resistance

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating importation and transmission risk
Vaccination coverage gaps post-COVID-19 pandemic have created susceptible cohorts
High transmissibility (R0 12-18) enables rapid spread in under-vaccinated communities
threats.action: Conduct vaccination coverage assessments; implement targeted catch-up immunization campaigns; strengthen laboratory confirmation capacity; enforce international health regulations at points of entry

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV Co-circulation
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses and Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: PAHO alerts in January 2026 and April 2026 highlight simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation stressing health systems
ECDC communicable disease threat reports through May 2026 track influenza activity across European region
Southern Hemisphere season onset April 2026 signals upcoming burden escalation
threats.action: Monitor hospital admission and ICU occupancy; promote influenza vaccination for high-risk groups; implement RSV prophylaxis protocols for vulnerable infants; coordinate antiviral stockpile readiness

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 2025 indicating cases in the Americas region
High case fatality rate (30-40%) in pulmonary syndrome presentations with no approved antiviral treatment
Rodent reservoir population dynamics linked to environmental and climate factors
threats.action: Enhance rodent control in endemic areas; educate at-risk rural and outdoor workers on exposure prevention; ensure ICU capacity for cardiopulmonary support; strengthen reporting from sentinel sites

selectAgentSummary: Three BSL-3/BSL-4 select agents are identified in this surveillance period. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) is a BSL-3 select agent with critical pandemic potential, flagged via two PAHO updates covering November 2025 and March 2026 for the Americas region. Monkeypox virus (Orthopoxvirus) is a BSL-3 select agent with confirmed ongoing human-to-human transmission in the Americas as of April 2026. Yellow fever virus, a BSL-3 select agent, generated a March 2026 PAHO epidemiological alert for the Americas. All three require enhanced biosafety containment protocols, specialized laboratory handling, and immediate notification to national public health authorities.
amrSignals: Potential macrolide-resistant Bordetella pertussis strains may be contributing to pertussis resurgence despite vaccination, warranting antimicrobial susceptibility surveillance
Influenza antiviral resistance (oseltamivir) monitoring warranted given high-volume treatment seasons across both hemispheres
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen respiratory season (influenza, RSV, pertussis) is compressing healthcare capacity across the Americas and Europe creating syndromic triage challenges

Repeated PAHO H5N1 alerts across a 4-month window (November 2025 to March 2026) suggest sustained and potentially expanding animal reservoir activity in the Americas increasing zoonotic spillover probability
Post-pandemic vaccination coverage gaps are enabling resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases including measles and pertussis across multiple WHO regions
Climate-driven vector range expansion is sustaining elevated dengue and chikungunya transmission beyond traditional endemic zones
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert reflects emerging non-infectious public health risk requiring pharmacovigilance integration into surveillance frameworks
Concurrent BSL-3 select agent activity (H5N1, Mpox, Yellow Fever) across the Americas represents an unusual multi-threat burden requiring coordinated biosafety and response resources
